    26	/**
    27	 * Stages, applies and recovers a full settings replace across the three stores.
    28	 *
    29	 * Usage: [stage] while the app runs; [startup] first thing in the next process, before Hilt-created stores,
    30	 * WorkManager or any screen reads settings.
    31	 *
    32	 * Invariants:
    33	 *  - CLAIM(stage-no-write): stage never changes a store; an invalid file changes nothing, and the only durable
    34	 *    write is the Staged journal record, after every check passed.
    35	 *  - CLAIM(domain-replace): apply removes catalog Configuration keys absent from the desired set and leaves every
    36	 *    other key (internal flags, usage counters, unknown keys) untouched. Destination automation is an import-reset
    37	 *    domain, separate from transferable configuration: the same preferences commit removes its credential and
    38	 *    receipts and writes enabled=false. Previous captures these raw values too, so rollback restores them exactly.
    39	 *  - CLAIM(journal-first): the Applying record, which holds previous and desired, is durable before the first
    40	 *    store changes.
    41	 *  - CLAIM(rollback-on-doubt): a thrown store failure or an interrupted Applying journal selects rollback.
    42	 *    Rollback restores every component from the journaled previous configuration, attempting all of them even
    43	 *    when one fails.
    44	 *  - CLAIM(all-or-previous): after startup returns a result that allows normal operation, every component holds
    45	 *    the desired configuration or every component holds the previous one.
    46	 *  - CLAIM(blocked-not-success): if rollback fails, the journal is unreadable or a journal write fails, the result
    47	 *    is RecoveryRequired and success is never reported. The last durable phase stays on disk: Applying and
    48	 *    RollingBack block normal operation and a later startup converges from them (Applying always rolls back).
    49	 *  - CLAIM(previous-raw): previous is captured at startup, not at staging, from the raw store content of every

    private fun buildLayout(): View {
        val column = LinearLayout(this).apply {
            orientation = LinearLayout.VERTICAL
            val pad = dp(16)
            setPadding(pad, pad, pad, pad)
        }
        fun add(view: View, setup: Boolean = false, action: Boolean = false): View {
            column.addView(view, LinearLayout.LayoutParams(ViewGroup.LayoutParams.MATCH_PARENT, ViewGroup.LayoutParams.WRAP_CONTENT))
            if (setup) setupViews += view
            return view
        }
        fun title(res: Int, setup: Boolean = true) = add(TextView(this).apply {
            setText(res); textSize = 18f; setPadding(0, dp(20), 0, dp(4))
        }, setup)
        fun body(res: Int, setup: Boolean = true) = add(TextView(this).apply { setText(res) }, setup)
        fun field(hint: Int, type: Int, maxLength: Int = 0): EditText = EditText(this).apply {
            setHint(hint); inputType = type
            if (maxLength > 0) filters = arrayOf(InputFilter.LengthFilter(maxLength))
        }.also { add(it, true) }
        fun button(text: Int, setup: Boolean = true, guarded: Boolean = false, onClick: () -> Unit): Button =
            Button(this).apply { setText(text); setOnClickListener { onClick() } }.also {
                add(it, setup)
                if (guarded) actionButtons += it
            }

        add(TextView(this).apply { setText(R.string.app_name); textSize = 24f })
        body(R.string.intro, setup = false)

New components are untouched, and `blockExtendsSnapshotForNewComponents` pins the snapshot extension before the new component's disable.
- **S2 resolved as a code and test finding.** The protocol, gate and coordinator are real production classes; the Android adapter has no branching beyond PackageManager calls and a `toInt` map. The owner can now act on the error. The Pixel 9a device check remains evidence, not a bar item.
- **S4 resolved.** The root build configured `:settings_portability` with the `jetbrainsKotlinJvm apply false` line present (attempt 1 and attempt 2 logs). Whether it would also have configured without the line is unknown and does not matter: the line is the conventional form and the build is observed to configure.

None at blocker or should. I looked for an in-scope failure in the new code and did not find one. What follows is a verification gate, not a defect.

The code I read reaches durability 9 only once four facts that no JVM test can establish have been observed. Two of the diff's lines (`FarhanApplication.kt:34`, `SettingsBackupActivity.kt:91`) are uncompiled, the production journal has never round-tripped a record on Android, and the Android component adapter has never executed. The protocol is correct on paper; the paper has to meet the phone once.

Gates, in the order that gives the most information per minute:

1. Full assemble of 9731cee for both APKs. Resolves the two uncompiled corrections.
2. Instrumented `AndroidImportJournal` test: every phase round-trips, including `previous` with raw values of the "wrong" type.
3. On the Pixel 9a (debuggable build): capture `dumpsys package ly.com.tahaben.farhan` component states; write garbage into `no_backup/settings_import_v1` with `run-as`; launch; confirm every normal component is disabled and the recovery icon appears; delete the garbage; launch; confirm `dumpsys` states equal the capture byte for byte and the recovery icon is gone. 4. Stage a real export, kill, relaunch, see Applied, acknowledge; then roll back once by making a store fail if that is cheap, otherwise accept the JVM rollback tests.

SCORE[error-paths]: 8/10 (fail-closed paths are pinned on the production classes; SOURCE_CHANGED advice is actionable; stashed nits only; bar 6)
SCORE[security]: 8/10 (no in-model exposure; three implied permissions removed from the helper; the `:acra` process no longer touches the journal; bar 6)
SCORE[architecture]: 8/10 (the port extraction is the right shape and the adapter stayed thin; root build configures; bar 6)
SCORE[legibility]: 8/10 (claims cite the test that proves them; two comment nits below; bar 6)

- app/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan/FarhanApplication.kt:32-33 CLAIM(recovery-single-process) cites a research report. Cite the observed source instead: `captures/settings/build-attempt2/evidence/app-manifest.xml:177-193` and the ACRA 5.12.0 `ACRA.kt` line.
- settings_portability/src/test/java/ly/com/tahaben/settings_portability/RecoveryComponentsTest.kt:146 `validate()` has a value case but no name case. A snapshot holding the marker name or a name without a dot is never rejected by a test. Add one line to `snapshotAndToggleFailuresRemainRecoverable`.

HARDENING-STASH:
- settings_rescue/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan_rescue/ui/RescueActivity.kt:515 On API 30 and later, `ACTION_NOTIFICATION_LISTENER_DETAIL_SETTINGS` with `EXTRA_NOTIFICATION_LISTENER_COMPONENT_NAME` opens the old Farhan's listener row directly. Polish only; the generic page works.
- settings_rescue/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan_rescue/capture/CaptureEngine.kt:92 (pre-existing) `throwIfCancelled` is tested in `CaptureEngineTest` but no production caller passes it; cancel works by killing the bridge process (CLAIM(real-cancel)).
